name: hmmscan with Pfam
compares: Each query protein against the curated profile models of every Pfam family, without searching any relative.
score: Domain bit score: higher ranks first. E-value cutoffs 10 (sequence and domain).
caveats: Pfam domains are defined by these same models, so scoring hmmscan against the Pfam truth set grades the models against their own output. Read its Pfam row as the best a search could do, not as a competitor.
It was scored against the Pfam truth set only. Swiss-Prot features and Pfam-N: not run.

known_failure_modes.finding: HMMER rounds E-values to two significant figures. Counting E ≤ cutoff on those rounded values, instead of E < cutoff, made the dark-set counts 2 to 222 lower. The dark set is the proteins that no search tool hits below the cutoff.

evidence.quote: The pipeline's own dark set uses E ≤ cutoff, and HMMER rounds E-values to two significant figures. Under that rule the dark counts are 2 to 222 lower; Botryllus at E ≤ 10 is 2_039.

known_failure_modes.run: notebook 289, dark set and kmerseek reach at E < 1 vs E < 10
known_failure_modes.what_to_do: Say whether each cutoff is strict (E < 1) or not (E ≤ 1), and use the same rule in every count that is compared.

licence: BSD 3-clause (HMMER); CC0 1.0 (Pfam-A models, per the Pfam 38.2 release notes)
questions: Is every family you expect to find already in Pfam? If no, this tool cannot find it: it only reports families that have a Pfam model.

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.785 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.802 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.871 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.580 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.573 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, no relative searched, setting Pfam models.)
Can you spend about 0.389 core-hours per 1,000 proteins? That is the measured cost of scanning them against Pfam's models.
